common_name: Rubinetta Skimmia (Compact Male Pollinator Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Site within about 15 feet of a female cultivar such as 'Nymans' or 'Veitchii' to ensure reliable berry set on those plants; Rubinetta itself sets no fruit.

directions: Rubinetta is a compact male selection valued strictly as a fragrant pollinator, since it carries no berries but opens masses of pink-flushed, wine-red buds that persist through winter before fading to white in spring. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, acidic to neutral soil in light to full shade, sheltering it from strong wind and midday sun that can scorch the glossy foliage. Its dense, rounded habit needs little pruning beyond removing any wayward shoots after flowering. Because it is dioecious like all Skimmia, this male clone will never produce berries itself, regardless of care.

common_name: Magic Marlot Skimmia (Variegated Male Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant purely for foliage color and fragrance, or as a pollinator for nearby female Skimmia japonica cultivars; it does not set berries itself.

directions: A sport of the male cultivar 'Marlot' discovered as a branch mutation in the Netherlands, Magic Marlot pairs typical fragrant white spring flowers and red winter buds with cream-margined, blue-green evergreen foliage that brightens shaded borders year-round. As a male clone it produces no berries but works well as a pollinator for nearby female Skimmia japonica cultivars. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in dappled or partial shade, since deep shade dulls the variegation while full sun can scorch the leaf margins. This slow-growing, compact form suits containers or small shaded beds where its foliage can be seen up close.

common_name: Kew White Skimmia (Female Evergreen Shrub with White Berries)

planting.note: Plant a male pollinator such as 'Kew Green', 'Rubella', or 'Fragrans' within about 15 feet, since this female cultivar sets no fruit on its own.

directions: Raised at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, this female cultivar bears clusters of fragrant white spring flowers that mature into unusually showy, creamy-white berries lasting from autumn into winter. It requires a nearby male pollinator to fruit, and pairs especially well against the dark evergreen foliage of red-berried companions. Grow in reliably moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in light to full shade, mulching annually to keep roots cool and conserve moisture. Its slow, dense growth habit makes it a long-term feature for a shaded border without regular pruning.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew plant records

common_name: Chelsea Physic Skimmia (Compact Fragrant Male Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Grown chiefly for fragrance and as a pollinator; site near female Skimmia japonica cultivars such as 'Nymans' or 'Kew White' to aid their berry set.

directions: Chelsea Physic is a compact male hybrid closely related to 'Kew Green' but smaller in every respect, producing dense clusters of intensely fragrant greenish-white flowers in early spring. Grown purely for scent and as a pollinator, it sets no berries but readily pollinates nearby female Skimmia japonica cultivars. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in light to full shade, sheltered from cold, drying winds that can brown the leaf edges. Its naturally tidy, rounded habit and slow growth suit it to small gardens, courtyards, and container culture near a path or door where its fragrance can be enjoyed.
